repository.name: bevy
repository.description: A refreshingly simple data-driven game engine built in Rust

issue.body:
# Objective

- Fix #10165 
- On iOS simulator on apple silicon Macs, shader validation is going through the host, but device limits are reported for the device. They sometimes differ, and cause the validation to crash on something that should work
```
-[MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder validateCommonDrawErrors:]:5775: failed assertion `Draw Errors Validation
Fragment Function(fragment_): the offset into the buffer _naga_oil_mod_MJSXM6K7OBRHEOR2NVSXG2C7OZUWK527MJUW4ZDJNZTXG_memberfog that is bound at buffer index 6 must be a multiple of 256 but was set to 448.
```

## Solution

- Add a custom flag when building for the simulator and override the buffer alignment

issue.title: Support iOS Simulator and Mac Catalyst

repository.name: wgpu
repository.description: A cross-platform, safe, pure-Rust graphics API.

issue.body:
## Problem

I often test iOS applications in the Simulator and on Mac Catalyst, since it's faster than pulling out a cable and connecting to a separate device.

Currently, though, [running Ruffle on the Simulator](https://github.com/madsmtm/ruffle-ios) fails with:
```
-[MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder validateCommonDrawErrors:]:5775: failed assertion `Draw Errors Validation
Vertex Function(main_vertex): the offset into the buffer transforms that is bound at buffer index 1 must be a multiple of 256 but was set to 128.
'
```

And I have to disable `Metal: API Validation` in the Xcode Scheme because Ruffle [assumes a specific alignment for uniform buffers](https://github.com/ruffle-rs/ruffle/blob/0821c11b11b232cf591f4ad5555692ac2a18b435/render/wgpu/src/buffer_builder.rs#L27-L31), which comes from [this piece of code that assumes 64 on iOS](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/ff4496b5d6011666bff6712258315a49af1fee5b/wgpu-hal/src/metal/adapter.rs#L728).


## Why does this happen

Fundamentally, this happens because the GPU hardware available on the Mac is different from the hardware available on the iPhone. In most cases, the iOS Simulator papers over differences between these two platforms, but when it comes to "low-level" interfacing with hardware (which Metal kind of _is_), we have to do work to handle this difference.

Luckily, the [iOS targets provided by `rustc`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/rustc/platform-support/apple-ios.html) are different depending on whether we're targetting the Simulator (`target_abi = "sim"`), Mac Catalyst (`target_abi = "macabi"`) or actual hardware (`target_abi = ""`).


## Desired solution

It would be nice if [`PrivateCapabilities::new` in `wgpu-hal/src/metal/adapter.rs`](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/blob/ff4496b5d6011666bff6712258315a49af1fee5b/wgpu-hal/src/metal/adapter.rs#L511-L869) was updated to fully support both the iOS Simulator and Mac Catalyst. See the following links for Apple's documentation on this:
- [Supporting Simulator in a Metal app](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/supporting-simulator-in-a-metal-app?language=objc)
- [Developing Metal apps that run in Simulator](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/developing-metal-apps-that-run-in-simulator?language=objc)

I would have filed a PR instead if I was certain of how, but I am not familiar enough with Metal to understand all the terms in there, so filing this as an issue first. I do know that you probably want the following different variables:
```rust
let is_mac = cfg!(target_os = "macos");
let mac_or_catalyst = cfg!(any(target_os = "macos", target_abi = "macabi"));
let runs_on_mac = cfg!(any(target_os = "macos", target_abi = "macabi", target_abi = "sim"));
let is_xr = cfg!(target_os = "visionos");
```

Also, semantically, it feels like `PrivateCapabilities::new` is trying to do two things: Detect the capabilities of the GPU, and detect the availability of certain APIs provided on newer OS versions. It might make sense to consider these separately? Because detecting the GPU capabilities probably means doing `if runs_on_mac || is_xr`, while detecting availability of APIs probably means using `if mac_or_catalyst || is_xr || version.at_least(...)`.

Feel free to tag me in a PR updating this, or ask me for further clarifications or testing, would be happy to help get this resolved!
